output.name: Mesil
output.myth: When the dark half is longest, the lamps along the Lamp Road burn low and smoke. Ennu the Kite-Wright, who keeps the lamp-wicks, takes up his shears of bone and sail-cord and climbs. Hesk at the pole counts the wicks as he goes. He cuts each one back so the flame comes up clean. At the Net Shuttle the old women's thread is still wet with winter, and he stops to watch it go under and over. Past the Bride-Kite he goes quickly, since her ribbons were cut once already. Then he hangs the shears in Vel for one night, so the people know the work is done. My grandmother saw them once, above the north shore. She said the blades were open like a bird's wings, and you could hear them in the wind if you were quiet. The next night they were gone. Tavo the Gale had come up the Leeward sea past the Knot that Would Not Loose, laughing, and carried them off to the Unflown, where he hides what he steals.
output.finding: Start at the Bride-Kite and go just under a hand-span south-east of it, along the Lamp Road, where Mesil's lamps burn.
